fields.name: requestBrand
fields.description: Request an asynchronous data fetching & processing of the given brand. If provided, once the process is complete, the callback URL will be called with the brand data.

fields.name: requestRefresh
fields.description: Request an asynchronous refresh (re-indexing) of the given brand. If provided, once the refresh is complete, the callback URL will be called with the updated brand data. A brand that was crawled within the past 24 hours cannot be refreshed again yet: the request is rejected with `success: false` and the code `recentlyCrawled`.

fields.name: createWebhook
fields.description: Creates and activates a new webhook

fields.name: updateWebhook
fields.description: Update the configuration of an existing webhook

fields.name: deleteWebhook
fields.description: Deactivates and removes a webhook

fields.name: addWebhookSubscriptions
fields.description:
Subscribe a webhook to the given URN.
This adds the URN to the scope list of URNs that the webhook will be notified about.
For example, passing the URN of a brand will cause the webhook to be notified of all changes to that brand.

fields.name: removeWebhookSubscriptions
fields.description:
Unsubscribe a webhook from the given URN.
This removes the URN from the scope list of URNs that the webhook will be notified about.

fields.name: updateProfile
fields.description:
Updates the authenticated user's own profile. A field that is omitted or `null` keeps its
current value; at least one field must be provided. Requires a user session — an API key
cannot act on a profile.

fields.name: deleteAccount
fields.description:
Permanently deletes the authenticated user's own account. This removes their sign-in
credentials, removes them from every organization they share with other members, and requests
deletion of any organization where they were the only member — which is processed
asynchronously and cascades to all associated data (billing records, API keys, clients,
webhooks, and so on).
If the user is the only member of an organization that cannot be deleted (it has termination
protection or is on a custom/enterprise plan), the request is rejected and nothing is changed.

fields.name: recordOrganizationAttribution
fields.description:
Records the Google Analytics ids of the visit this organization grew out of.
First touch wins: once recorded the pair is never overwritten, so the dashboard can
send this on every sign-in. The ids are read back when a checkout link is created,
which is what attributes a purchase to the campaign that brought the organization
in — even when the member who buys is not the member who signed up.

fields.name: deleteOrganization
fields.description: Requests deletion of the organization. Deletion is processed asynchronously and, once complete, permanently removes the organization and all of its associated data (API keys, clients, members, invitations, billing, webhooks, etc.).

Name of that API client at the time of reading. Included because the log covers
revoked clients too, and those are absent from `Organization.apiClients`.

fields.name: path

fields.name: domain
fields.description: Brand domain (or asset id) the request resolved to.

fields.name: assetType
fields.description: Asset kind — `logo`, `icon`, `symbol`, …

fields.name: format
fields.description: Delivered image format — `webp`, `png`, `svg`, …

fields.name: bytes

fields.name: cacheResult

fields.name: referer

fields.name: countryCode
fields.description:
Two-letter country the request came from, resolved from the client IP. A
`String` rather than the `CountryCode` scalar, because an unrecognized value is
reported as-is instead of failing the page.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: Datetime when the item was created

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: Datetime when the item was last updated

fields.name: createdBy
fields.description: The Actor who created the organization. Null when that account no longer exists.

fields.name: billingCountryCode
fields.description:
Two-letter ISO 3166-1 code of the country the organization is billed in. Always null at
present: no billing country is recorded against an organization.

fields.name: invitations
fields.description: All pending invitations to join this organization

fields.name: users
fields.description: Get a list of all users in this organization.

fields.name: apiKeys
fields.description: Get a list of all API Keys for this organization.

fields.name: apiClients
fields.description: Get a list of all Clients for this organization.

types.name: PageInfo
types.description: Pagination information

fields.name: endCursor
fields.description: An end cursor for use in pagination.

fields.name: hasNextPage
fields.description: Indicates if there are more pages to fetch.

fields.name: hasPreviousPage
fields.description: Indicates if there are any pages prior to the current page.

fields.name: startCursor
fields.description: An start cursor for use in pagination.

fields.name: totalPages

fields.name: currentPage
fields.description: The current page.

types.name: QuotaUsage
types.description:
Consumption of one quota, and what is left to spend against it.
`currentPeriod.quota` is the recurring allowance alone. It is not what an organization
may spend: one-time credits and any overage allowance count towards that too, and a
plan can carry no recurring allowance at all. Read `credits` for what is spendable.

fields.name: credits
fields.description:
What the organization can still spend against this quota, and whether it is currently
being billed for overage.
Reported for the organization even on an individual API key or client, because
allowances are held at the organization level and shared by its keys. A key's own
`currentPeriod.used` counts only that key's requests.

types.name: ApiCredits
types.description:
An organization's spendable allowance for one quota.
Spent in a fixed order: the recurring allowance first, then any overage allowance, then
one-time credits — so credits are drawn on last and carry over until they are used.

fields.name: available
fields.description:
Requests still available in this period: what is left of the recurring allowance and
the overage allowance, plus `prepaidBalance`. -1 when the allowance is unlimited.

fields.name: prepaidBalance
fields.description:
One-time credits still held. Unlike the recurring allowance these do not expire at the
end of a period and are not replenished automatically. 0 for quotas that do not use
one-time credits.

fields.name: overageAllowance
fields.description:
Requests permitted beyond the recurring allowance, funded by the organization's overage
limit. 0 when no overage limit is set, and for quotas that are not billed for overage.
This is what the limit pays for, which is not always spendable: an overage allowance is
only counted towards `available` while payment on the subscription is up to date.

fields.name: isOveraging
fields.description: Whether requests in this period are currently being billed at the overage rate.

fields.name: overageRequests
fields.description: Requests billed at the overage rate so far in this period, up to `overageAllowance`.

fields.name: overageAmount
fields.description:
`overageRequests` priced at the overage rate, in the same currency as
`Organization.hardOverageDollarLimit`.

fields.name: renewsAt
fields.description:
When the recurring allowance next resets. Null when the quota has no recurring
allowance to reset, as for an organization funded entirely by one-time credits.

fields.name: quota
fields.description: The recurring allowance for the period. -1 means unlimited.

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByURL`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description: Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and optionally a default value.

fields.name: defaultValue
fields.description: A GraphQL-formatted string representing the default value for this input value.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

enumValues.name: QUERY
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a query operation.

enumValues.name: MUTATION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a mutation operation.

enumValues.name: SUBSCRIPTION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a subscription operation.

enumValues.name: FIELD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment definition.

enumValues.name: FRAGMENT_SPREAD
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a fragment spread.

enumValues.name: INLINE_FRAGMENT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an inline fragment.

enumValues.name: VARIABLE_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a variable definition.

enumValues.name: SCHEMA
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a schema definition.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a scalar definition.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an object type definition.

enumValues.name: FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a field definition.

enumValues.name: ARGUMENT_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an argument definition.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an interface definition.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to a union definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum definition.

enumValues.name: ENUM_VALUE
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an enum value definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object type definition.

enumValues.name: INPUT_FIELD_DEFINITION
enumValues.description: Location adjacent to an input object field definition.

directives.name: include
directives.description: Directs the executor to include this field or fragment only when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: skip
directives.description: Directs the executor to skip this field or fragment when the `if` argument is true.

directives.name: deprecated
directives.description: Marks an element of a GraphQL schema as no longer supported.

args.name: reason
args.description: Explains why this element was deprecated, usually also including a suggestion for how to access supported similar data. Formatted using the Markdown syntax, as specified by [CommonMark](https://commonmark.org/).

directives.name: specifiedBy
directives.description: Exposes a URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.

args.name: url
args.description: The URL that specifies the behavior of this scalar.
